C1.worst_defect: The home page says what it is and where to click, but nothing tells a merchant who should not use it or how it differs from a hosted till. A merchant with integrated card terminals, coupon-driven promotions or MySQL only finds out from scattered bullets under 'Before you start' or a link to Limitations; there is no 'not for you if…' line.
C1.where: home.desktop.01-02 / text/home.txt ('What it does today', 'Before you start')

C2.worst_defect: The home page and JSON-LD sell it as 'MIT licensed' and 'open-source' (isAccessibleForFree: true). Only a paragraph deep in Connect a till admits that 'Building it yourself needs your own RxDB Premium licence token', a paid proprietary dependency. Neither the home page nor Limitations mentions it. Separately, refunds and customer notes are shown in the demo but need 'a plugin release after 0.3.0, which is not out yet', and the changelog's last release is 2026-10-06 with no date for the next one.
C2.where: connect-a-till.desktop.01 ('Where your data goes', 2nd paragraph) vs home.desktop.02 footer and tech.json home JSON-LD; at-the-till.txt 'Refund a sale'; changelog.desktop.01

C3.worst_defect: Step 3 gives three migration routes in one paragraph: a tsx generate script, 'npx vendure migrate', and the plugin's bundled migrations, which plugin-setup offers instead. 'Review the generated migration and include it in config.dbConnectionOptions.migrations' shows no code for the include, so a developer has to guess which route is recommended and how to wire it up.

C4.worst_defect: The pages disagree about what 'plugin out of date' means. Troubleshooting says the store only needs 'order.create v4 and register v1, as every plugin release from 0.1.0 does'. At the till says 'Charges need plugin 0.3.0', and Notifications lists 'fee and shipping charges' as held back. Limitations also leaves out the unreleased customer note and the RxDB Premium build requirement.
C4.where: troubleshooting.desktop.01 ('Store settings') vs at-the-till.desktop.01 ('Add a charge') and notifications.desktop.01

C5.worst_defect: On every desktop docs page the grey sidebar panel stops at about y=900 and the page background shows below it, so the left rail looks cut off. The home hero's till screenshot is also cropped through a row of product cards at its bottom edge.
C5.where: docs.desktop.01, limitations.desktop.01, changelog.desktop.01 (left column below the GitHub/theme bar); home.desktop.01 hero image

C6.worst_defect: The hero till screenshot shrinks to unreadable 5-6 px text on a 390 px screen, so the only product visual proves nothing on a phone. Code blocks wrap mid-token, for example './vendure-' / 'config' and the CORS origin array split across lines. The quick-start phone capture is clipped (tech.json clipped: true; slice 09 ends at 'Optional: a device key for').
C6.where: home.phone.01 hero image; quick-start.phone.02-04 code blocks; quick-start.phone.09

C7.worst_defect: The 404 page reuses the home page's meta description ('Open-source point of sale for Vendure. Sell from the browser…') and has no JSON-LD. Docs pages carry only BreadcrumbList structured data, with no TechArticle or SoftwareApplication link back. Lighthouse, llms.txt, sitemap, robots and search are all fine.

overall_worst.defect: The home page sells it as 'MIT licensed' and open-source, but self-hosting the till needs a paid RxDB Premium licence token. That fact appears only mid-paragraph on Connect a till and is missing from the home page and from Limitations. I would flag that to a client as an undisclosed open-core catch.
overall_worst.where: connect-a-till.desktop.01 ('Building it yourself needs your own RxDB Premium licence token') vs home.desktop.02 footer 'MIT licensed' and limitations.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Add a Limitations bullet and one line in the home page's 'Before you start': 'The hosted till at app.vendurepos.com is free; building the till yourself needs a paid RxDB Premium licence.' Link both to the Connect a till paragraph.
